<summary>

  <investigated>Examined the OrderQuery pagination calculation and the related OrderQuery test for first-page positioning.</investigated>
  <learned>The extra subtraction of 1 in OrderQuery.pageOffset incorrectly shifted every page backward; the offset should simply equal page multiplied by page size.</learned>
  <completed>Updated OrderQuery.pageOffset to return `page * size` without the extra `-1`. Verified that OrderQueryTest#firstPageStartsAtZero passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue with any remaining pagination test coverage or related verification requested in the ongoing session.</next_steps>
  <notes>The bugfix is narrowly scoped and directly resolves the first-page offset failure.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in UserCache and verify that concurrent cache access no longer overwrites values with null placeholders.</request>
  <investigated>Examined UserCache.get and its concurrent loading behavior, then reviewed the CacheConcurrencyTest result after applying the change.</investigated>
  <learned>The previous get implementation could allow two concurrent callers to observe and write null placeholders. Using computeIfAbsent makes cache initialization atomic within the map computation, preventing competing null writes.</learned>
  <completed>Updated UserCache.get to load values through computeIfAbsent. The edit was applied successfully, and CacheConcurrencyTest now passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue the active bugfix trajectory by checking for any remaining related test failures, reviewing the final diff, and confirming the broader test suite still passes.</next_steps>
  <notes>The race was isolated to concurrent cache loading in UserCache; the concurrency-specific regression test validates the fix.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in UserCache and verify the change with the relevant concurrency test.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java, focusing on the get method and its cache-loading logic.</investigated>
  <learned>The previous implementation using cache.get(id) followed by a placeholder write allowed concurrent callers to observe missing entries and race. Using computeIfAbsent with the loader atomically ensures only one caller performs the load and prevents duplicate null-placeholder writes.</learned>
  <completed>Changed UserCache.get to load entries through cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load). The edit was applied successfully, and CacheConcurrencyTest passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions beyond CacheConcurrencyTest.</next_steps>
  <notes>The targeted race-condition test currently passes; full-suite results remain to be confirmed.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in UserCache caused by concurrent cache misses potentially overwriting a null placeholder, then verify the fix.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java and compared the previous get implementation, which directly called cache.get(id), with an atomic computeIfAbsent-based loading approach.</investigated>
  <learned>Using computeIfAbsent ensures only one concurrent caller loads and stores a missing value, preventing duplicate loads and avoiding the race that could leave a null placeholder in the cache.</learned>
  <completed>Updated UserCache.get to load missing entries through cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load). The focused CacheConcurrencyTest passes, confirming the concurrent-access behavior is corrected.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions beyond CacheConcurrencyTest.</next_steps>
  <notes>The code change is complete and the targeted concurrency test has passed; only broader project verification remains.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in UserCache so concurrent cache misses cannot both write a null placeholder, then verify the fix.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java, focusing on the cache retrieval and loading logic in UserCache.get.</investigated>
  <learned>The previous implementation returned cache.get(id), which allowed separate missing-value and loader operations to race. Using computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load) atomically loads absent values and prevents concurrent callers from writing conflicting null placeholders.</learned>
  <completed>Updated UserCache.get to use cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load). The targeted CacheConcurrencyTest now passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions beyond the targeted concurrency test.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix is localized to UserCache.get, and the targeted concurrency test confirms that the reported race is resolved.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix and regression-test the DailyReport off-by-one-day issue caused by using UTC instead of the business timezone.</request>
  <investigated>The DailyReport business-date behavior was exercised at the UTC-to-Asia/Shanghai date boundary, specifically around 2026-11-01T23:30Z.</investigated>
  <learned>A report timestamp near midnight UTC can fall on a different calendar date in Asia/Shanghai. The expected business date for 2026-11-01T23:30Z is 2026-11-02, confirming that timezone-aware date calculation is required.</learned>
  <completed>Added DailyReportTest#reportUsesBusinessTimezone to pin the timezone-boundary behavior. The test reproduces the reported off-by-one-day bug and passes after the fix.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue validating the DailyReport timezone fix and run the relevant test suite to check for regressions.</next_steps>
  <notes>The regression test explicitly covers the Asia/Shanghai business timezone and the date transition from November 1 to November 2, 2026.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix CsvExporter line-ending handling so multiline CSV fields do not cause incorrect row counts.</request>
  <investigated>The CSV export behavior and regression coverage around multiline fields were examined, focusing on embedded line endings and their interaction with quoting.</investigated>
  <learned>Embedded line endings must be normalized before field quoting; normalizing them to CRLF preserves the exporter’s expected CSV row structure when fields contain multiple lines.</learned>
  <completed>Updated CsvExporter to normalize embedded line endings to CRLF before quoting. Confirmed that CsvExporterTest#multilineFieldKeepsRowCount passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue validating the CSV exporter change, including relevant existing test coverage and any additional edge cases involving embedded line endings.</next_steps>
  <notes>The implemented fix is localized to CsvExporter and directly addresses multiline fields being counted as multiple CSV rows.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix CSV exporter line endings so multiline fields preserve the correct row count and use consistent CRLF output.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/export/CsvExporter.java, focusing on how embedded newline characters are processed before fields are quoted.</investigated>
  <learned>Embedded fields can contain mixed LF and CRLF line endings. Normalising those endings to CRLF before quoting ensures consistent CSV output and prevents multiline content from being misinterpreted as additional rows.</learned>
  <completed>Updated CsvExporter to replace embedded line endings using writer.write(line.replaceAll("\\r?\\n", "\\r\\n")). The focused regression test CsvExporterTest#multilineFieldKeepsRowCount now passes.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions across the project.</next_steps>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in CounterService and verify concurrent counter increments are correct.</request>
  <investigated>CounterService.increment was identified as using a non-atomic read-then-write sequence on the counter, creating a race under concurrent access. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest was used to validate the behavior with 1000 threads.</investigated>
  <learned>Using AtomicLong.incrementAndGet performs a single atomic increment and eliminates the lost-update race caused by separate get and set operations.</learned>
  <completed>Updated CounterService.increment to use AtomicLong.incrementAndGet. CounterServiceConcurrencyTest now passes with 1000 concurrent increments producing a final count of 1000.</completed>
  <next_steps>Continue with any requested follow-up verification or related concurrency checks; no additional work is currently pending based on the available observations.</next_steps>
  <notes>The fix is applied and the relevant concurrency test is green.</notes>
</summary>

<summary>
  <request>Fix the race condition in CounterService and verify the concurrent counter behavior.</request>
  <investigated>Inspected src/main/java/com/acme/metrics/CounterService.java and identified the non-atomic get/set increment pattern used by CounterService.increment.</investigated>
  <learned>The previous counter.set(counter.get() + 1) implementation could lose increments when multiple threads updated the value concurrently. Replacing it with AtomicLong.incrementAndGet provides an atomic increment.</learned>
  <completed>Updated CounterService.increment to use counter.incrementAndGet() instead of counter.set(counter.get() + 1). Verified with CounterServiceConcurrencyTest: 1,000 concurrent threads produced a final count of 1,000, and the test passed.</completed>
  <next_steps>Run the full verification suite to check for regressions and confirm the complete project remains green.</next_steps>
  <notes>The targeted concurrency regression test passes. The code change is limited to making the counter increment atomic.</notes>
</summary>

</summary>
